summary: Steel tower, 80 ft, built 1937 in Hillsborough County; removal bids in 2009-10, then sold at auction for $860. No source describes the site now.

events.note: A 1972 Tampa Times item quoted on the site says the towers were built in 1937; it calls Brown identical to four other Hillsborough County towers.
Laura Leavine named as towerwoman in a November 1950 list of Hillsborough County observation towers.
April 1956 report: Sylvia Beasley to operate the tower, with Frank Beasley as assistant ranger, replacing a couple transferred to Sarasota County.
Invitation to bid on removal of the tower issued September 2009; bid opening 8 October 2009; no award made.
Second invitation to bid for removal of the 80-foot steel tower, March 2010; bid opening 28 April 2010.
Sold at auction for $860.00 in April 2010. The page does not say whether the tower was then taken down.

notes_for_editor: One compiled source: a regional lookout site that quotes a 1950 Tampa Tribune list, an April 1956 Tampa Tribune item, an October 1972 Tampa Times item and county bid notices from 2009 and 2010. The newspapers were not checked directly. Sources disagree on location: Bullfrog Creek on Road 41 (1950), U.S. 301 south of Riverview (1956), northeast of Ruskin (1972); the story gives all three. The April 2010 auction sale does not confirm removal, and no source found describes the site now; the status, access and staffing fields stay unknown. Two web searches found nothing more about this tower. The National Historic Lookout Register lists Hamner Tower, a Hillsborough County tower it dates to 1937 and calls standing; it may be one of the 1972 'identical' towers, but this was not checked and is not used in the story.
